summary: Saved dashboard view reverts to compacted timeseries after retention compaction causing missing trace links and suppressed alerts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that a saved dashboard view they rely on for daily monitoring started showing compacted/aggregated timeseries after a scheduled retention compaction job. The view no longer preserves the original per-request granularity, trace links on spike points are missing, and associated threshold alerts did not fire for a sustained error increase. This began after last night's rolling compaction window and affects a small set of org-scoped saved views.
impact: Several on-call engineers at the customer missed a material error spike because the saved dashboard reverted to compacted rollups. Business impact: delayed incident detection for production ingestion pipelines; customer requests urgent remediation and a postmortem of the retention compaction run that coincided with the regression.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to FinSage org in Console (prod/us-east)
2) Open saved dashboard 'Ingest - Request Latency (per-request) - FinSage-prod' at 2026-03-11T22:00:00Z to 2026-03-11T23:00:00Z
3) Observe time-series appears as hourly rollups rather than per-request points; trace link icons are absent on spike markers
4) Reopen the same dashboard after toggling the timepicker to a different range and back; view remains compacted
5) Query raw events for the same interval via /usage-export endpoint and confirm high error rate present in raw events but not reflected in the dashboard alert history.
expected_behavior: Saved dashboard view should preserve the original granularity and show per-request points for ranges within retention boundaries. Trace links should be present on data points to navigate to traces, and alerts tied to that panel should evaluate against the raw/expected granularity so incidents surface appropriately.
actual_behavior: Saved view shows compacted hourly rollups; trace link icons are missing on those points; alert evaluation window skipped firing for the error spike. Other ad-hoc queries and raw exports show the events exist at full granularity.
logs: Console query id=qry-9f2a: returned series with rollup_bucket=3600 for metric ingest.requests.latency for 2026-03-11T22:00Z..23:00Z
Retention compaction job id=comp-20260311-A completed at 2026-03-11T23:47Z; compaction config: hourly_rollup=true, preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false
Trace link resolver returned 404 when asked to expand anchor for series point id=pt-7a8b due to missing point-level index
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Maya): customer saved view appears to be executed against the rollup table rather than the raw event index. Confirmed raw events are present via usage-export for the same interval.

SRE note (Liam): retention compaction run last night included a change that inadvertently caused saved dashboard materialized queries to point at rollup shards for certain org-scoped dashboards. Hypothesis: a mapping rewrite in compaction metadata introduced in rollback-commit rfc/compact-optim-2 changed view-to-table resolution.
Query debug: panel query uses alias 'events_main' which post-compaction resolves to events_rollup_3600 for time ranges older than 1 hour despite panel granularity config set to 'auto'.

Trace linking: link anchors rely on per-event index ids which are purged or not referenced in the rollup table; resolver fallback should attempt to map rollup buckets to representative events but that path returned no candidates.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Logged on with customer to reproduce. Confirmed mismatch between dashboard panel and raw export. Customer is on enterprise plan and requests priority handling.

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Marking as P1 Sev1. Assigning to SRE retention on-call. I've pulled compaction logs and see comp-20260311-A. Noted setting preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false — this looks like the trigger.

2026-03-11 SRE retention (Zoë Patel): Running a narrow rollback of compaction metadata mapping. Temporarily toggling preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=true for FinSage org to validate. ETA 45m.

2026-03-11 Maya Chen: Customer confirmed after metadata toggle that saved dashboard now shows per-request points for the sampled interval. Trace links reappeared on spike markers. They still want a root cause and prevention plan.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Patch prepared to ensure saved-view resolution prefers raw index if panel granularity != rollup interval. PR queued for code review: console-backend#1189. Scheduling hotfix deploy to prod/us-east with feature-flagged guard for backward compatibility.
resolution: Workaround applied: compaction metadata toggle enabled to preserve per-request granularity for affected saved views for FinSage org. Hotfix PR created and tested; rollout scheduled to prod/us-east with feature flag. Longer-term: compaction job will be updated to maintain mapping for org-scoped saved views by default and include integration test coverage.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Hotfix deployed to prod/us-east behind feature flag. Monitored 2 hours for regressions; no new incidents observed. Follow-up action items: add integration test for saved-view resolution in compaction pipeline, update runbook to avoid setting preserve_high_granularity_for_saved_views=false without org opt-in, and communicate to customers who may be affected. Postmortem draft assigned to INT-7890.
follow_up_actions: Create integration test that asserts saved dashboards resolve to raw index when panel granularity requires per-request points (owner: QA)
Update compaction runbook to include a preflight check for org-scoped saved views (owner: SRE)
Communicate with affected customers and offer remediation credit if incident caused missed alerts (owner: CS)
Attach postmortem to this ticket and link INT-7890
